content:
BurgerQuick Systems - Integration Architecture Overview
Version 9.0 | Oracle ADF 12c | Oracle Database 19c

PURPOSE
This document catalogs every system boundary where the BurgerQuick monolith exchanges data with an external party or out-of-process component. BurgerQuick is the operational backbone for a 200+ location quick-service restaurant chain processing 10,000+ orders/day across POS, web, mobile, and delivery channels.

The application is database-centric: PL/SQL packages in Oracle Database 19c own all business logic. The Java/ADF tier is presentation and data binding. Integrations therefore originate from BOTH the PL/SQL layer (queues, payment refs) AND the Java/ADF layer (outbound REST, JAX-RS endpoints).

EXTERNAL & CROSS-PROCESS INTEGRATIONS (summary)

1. HR SaaS (outbound REST) - Employee master data is mirrored to a third-party HR SaaS platform at burgerquick.hr-domain.com whenever an employee record changes in the ADF Employee Directory. Synchronous PUT, API-key auth.

2. Stripe (outbound, payment gateway) - Card payments for web and mobile orders are tokenized by Stripe. The Stripe token flows into API_ORDER_SERVICE.api_create_order and is persisted as payment_type='STRIPE'. Introduced in the 2018 'modernization' initiative.

3. PayPal (outbound, payment reference) - Legacy 2009 web-ordering channel records PayPal payment references on ONLINE_ORDERS.payment_ref (also used for last-4 of card). Reconciliation is manual.

4. In-store POS system (system-to-system push) - Web and mobile orders are pushed into the originating store's point-of-sale system so kitchen staff see them. Implemented by re-calling the legacy sp_OrderProcessing.sp_create_order path from WEB_ORDER_PKG.

5. RabbitMQ - inventory-updater microservice (async messaging) - A standalone Spring Boot service (inventory-updater) consumes 'inventory-update-queue' from RabbitMQ and writes inventory adjustments back into the Oracle database. Out-of-process from the monolith.

6. Oracle Advanced Queuing (AQ) - delivery lifecycle (internal async messaging) - Two AQ queues (inv_delivery_queue, inv_broadcast_queue) drive the inventory-delivery dashboard via a PL/SQL notification callback.

7. Order REST API (inbound, JAX-RS) - OrderRestController exposes /api/orders to the BurgerQuick mobile app and partner integrators. Wraps API_ORDER_SERVICE.

8. Mobile push notifications (outbound, PLANNED/STUB) - Loyalty point sync is meant to push to mobile devices; currently only stores a device_token. No push provider wired yet.

9. USER_SERVICE microservice (ABANDONED) - A 2018 attempt to extract a REST user-service onto its own normalized schema. Schema created, never populated, no live traffic. Listed for completeness.

DATA CLASSIFICATION
- HR SaaS carries PII (names, pay rate). 
- Stripe/PayPal carry payment data (tokens/refs only; no PAN stored).
- REST API carries order + customer identifiers.

fileName: HR SaaS Employee Sync - Interface Spec.docx
content:
Interface Specification: HR SaaS Employee Sync
Owner: People Systems team | Status: ACTIVE in production

OVERVIEW
When a manager edits an employee in the ADF Employee Directory, BurgerQuick mirrors the change to the company's external HR SaaS provider so payroll and benefits stay in sync. This is a fire-and-forget outbound integration; failures are logged but do not block the local save.

DIRECTION: Outbound (BurgerQuick -> HR SaaS)
PROTOCOL: HTTPS REST
IMPLEMENTED IN: ViewController/src/view/beans/util/HrSaasClient.java (called from the Employee Directory managed bean on update)

ENDPOINT
  Method: PUT
  Base URL: https://burgerquick.hr-domain.com/api/employee/
  Full path: https://burgerquick.hr-domain.com/api/employee/{employeeId}/update

AUTHENTICATION
  Header: X-Api-Key: <static API key>
  NOTE (risk): the API key is hard-coded as a constant in HrSaasClient.java. Should be moved to a credential store / WebLogic credential mapper.

TIMEOUTS
  Connect: 3000 ms
  Read: 3000 ms

REQUEST BODY (application/json):
  {
    "id": "<employeeId>",
    "firstName": "...",
    "lastName": "...",
    "position": "...",
    "hourlyRate": 18.50,
    "storeNumber": "..."
  }

RESPONSE HANDLING
  Any non-2xx status is logged as a WARNING ('HR SaaS update failed for employee <id>: HTTP <status>'). No retry, no dead-letter. IOExceptions are swallowed and logged.

FAILURE MODES / KNOWN GAPS
  - No retry or queue: a transient HR SaaS outage silently drops the update; local and remote drift until the next edit.
  - Synchronous call on the request thread (3s+3s) can stall the ADF save under HR SaaS latency.
  - PII (employee name + pay rate) crosses the boundary in clear JSON over TLS only.

fileName: Payments - Stripe and PayPal Integration Notes.md
content:
Payment Integrations - Stripe & PayPal

BurgerQuick takes card payments on two channels through two different processors, added in two different eras. There is no unified payment abstraction; each channel calls its processor's flow directly.

=== STRIPE (web + mobile, added 2018) ===
Direction: Outbound (BurgerQuick -> Stripe)
Type: Payment gateway / card tokenization
Flow:
  1. The mobile app / web front end collects card details and exchanges them with Stripe client-side for a single-use payment TOKEN. Raw card numbers never touch BurgerQuick.
  2. The token is sent to the inbound Order REST API and on to PL/SQL:
       API_ORDER_SERVICE.api_create_order(..., p_payment_token IN VARCHAR2, ...)
     which calls WEB_ORDER_PKG.place_online_order with:
       p_payment_type => 'STRIPE'
       p_payment_ref  => p_payment_token   (the Stripe token)
  3. The token/charge id is stored on the order row as the payment reference.
Defined in: Model/database/2018_modernization/01_api_order_service.sql, Model/database/2009_web_ordering/02_web_order_pkg.sql
Notes: This was the flagship deliverable of the 2018 'modernization'. Refund and webhook (charge.succeeded / dispute) handling were never implemented - settlement is reconciled manually in the Stripe dashboard.

=== PAYPAL (legacy web ordering, 2009) ===
Direction: Outbound (BurgerQuick -> PayPal)
Type: Payment reference capture
Flow: The 2009 web-ordering channel records a PayPal reference in ONLINE_ORDERS.payment_ref. The same column doubles as 'last 4 digits' for card orders (see comment in 2009_web_ordering/01_tables_customers_online.sql: 'Last 4 digits or PayPal ref'). payment_type distinguishes them.
Notes: No live API callback; this is essentially a stored external reference for reconciliation. Considered legacy; new volume goes through Stripe.

DATA: Only tokens / references are persisted. No PAN, no CVV. PCI scope is reduced to the token boundary.

Inventory Updater Microservice - RabbitMQ Integration
Module: inventory-updater (standalone Spring Boot service, Java)

WHY IT EXISTS
Inventory adjustments produced elsewhere in the BurgerQuick ecosystem are delivered asynchronously so the monolith and the database are not blocked. A small out-of-process Spring Boot consumer drains a RabbitMQ queue and applies the adjustments to the Oracle database.

MESSAGE BROKER: RabbitMQ
Direction: Inbound to the service (BurgerQuick / publishers -> RabbitMQ -> inventory-updater)
Queue name: inventory-update-queue (durable)
Message format: JSON (Jackson2JsonMessageConverter)
Acknowledge mode: manual

CONNECTION (from inventory-updater/src/main/resources/application.properties and docker-compose.yml):
  spring.rabbitmq.host=localhost
  spring.rabbitmq.port=5672
  spring.rabbitmq.username=guest
  spring.rabbitmq.password=guest
  Management UI: http://localhost:15672
  Broker image: rabbitmq:3-management

CONSUMER: com.burgerquick.inventoryupdater.InventoryUpdateConsumer
  Listens on inventory-update-queue, deserializes the JSON message, and persists the inventory change.

DOWNSTREAM DATABASE (second integration of this service):
  This service also connects directly to the Oracle DB (system/Oracle123!) via JDBC:
  jdbc:oracle:thin:@//localhost:1521/ORCLPDB1
  spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none (it does not own the schema; it writes into the monolith's tables).

KNOWN GAPS / RISKS
  - guest/guest broker credentials and a plaintext DB password (Oracle123!) committed in application.properties.
  - Manual ack but no visible dead-letter / retry policy in config; a poison message could block the consumer.
  - The service writes into tables owned by the monolith - shared-database coupling, not a true microservice boundary.

Delivery Lifecycle Messaging - Oracle Advanced Queuing (AQ)
Package: DELIVERY_ENHANCEMENT_PKG | Schema: 2026_delivery_enhancement

The inventory-supply delivery feature uses Oracle AQ (in-database messaging) to drive a near-real-time dashboard. This is an internal, in-database integration but crosses a process/async boundary, so it is inventoried here.

QUEUES
  1. inv_delivery_queue  - single-consumer WORK queue. One message per delivery, enqueued with status_at_enqueue='PENDING'. The message acts as a lock and is dequeued by aq_msg_id during fulfillment.
  2. inv_broadcast_queue - multi-consumer PUB/SUB queue. A new message is broadcast on every status transition (PENDING / COMPLETED / CANCELLED).

SUBSCRIBERS on inv_broadcast_queue
  - DASHBOARD_METRICS_AGENT  (ACTIVE) - async AQ notification wired to the PL/SQL callback sync_dashboard_metrics_cb.
  - DELIVERY_FULFILLMENT_AGENT (PLACEHOLDER, not implemented).

CALLBACK: sync_dashboard_metrics_cb (AQ notification callback)
  PENDING   -> pending += 1
  COMPLETED -> pending -= 1, fulfilled += 1
  CANCELLED -> pending -= 1
  Updates the DASHBOARD_STATS pre-aggregation table.

MESSAGE FLOW
  Create delivery : row inserted status='PENDING'; one message enqueued to BOTH queues.
  Fulfill delivery: inventory updated; status->'COMPLETED'; work-queue message dequeued by aq_msg_id; new COMPLETED message broadcast.
  Cancel delivery : status->'CANCELLED'; new CANCELLED broadcast. KNOWN GAP: the original work-queue message is never dequeued on cancel (orphaned lock message).

WHY THE DASHBOARD ALSO POLLS
  Delivering AQ callbacks requires job_queue_processes > 0 (Oracle background jobs). In dev this is often 0, so DashboardBean bypasses the callback and queries INVENTORY_DELIVERIES directly every 3 seconds. The AQ-fed DASHBOARD_STATS table and the direct poll can therefore disagree.

SOURCE: Model/database/2026_delivery_enhancement/02_delivery_enhancement_pkg.sql, 03_dashboard_metrics_aq.sql

Order REST API - Inbound JAX-RS Endpoints
Consumers: BurgerQuick mobile app; partner/integration clients
Direction: Inbound (clients -> BurgerQuick)
Introduced: 2018 modernization ('put REST APIs in front of everything')

IMPLEMENTATION
  JAX-RS controller: Model/src/model/rest/OrderRestController.java
    Base path: @Path("/api/orders")
    POST /api/orders/create   (Consumes/Produces application/json) - create an order
    GET  /api/orders/{orderId}/status - fetch order status
  Delivery controller: Model/src/model/rest/DeliveryController.java (delivery endpoints)

These controllers are thin: they delegate to the PL/SQL REST wrapper package API_ORDER_SERVICE, which in turn calls the legacy stored procedures.

PL/SQL WRAPPER: API_ORDER_SERVICE (Model/database/2018_modernization/01_api_order_service.sql)
  api_create_order(p_customer_id, p_store_id, p_items_json, p_payment_token, OUT p_order_id, OUT p_status)
    - p_items_json: real JSON order lines
    - p_payment_token: Stripe token (see Payments doc) -> stored payment_type='STRIPE'
  api_get_order_status(p_order_id, p_order_source IN ('POS','WEB','MOBILE'), OUT p_status, OUT p_details cursor)
  api_find_order(p_order_id) RETURN SYS_REFCURSOR - unified lookup across POS/web/mobile

INTEGRATION SIGNIFICANCE
  - This is the single inbound API surface for mobile ordering; it bridges modern JSON clients to 2003-era PL/SQL order procedures.
  - 'Phase 2' (a standalone order microservice with its own DB) was planned but never built - the API still fronts the monolith.

KNOWN GAPS
  - No documented authentication/authorization layer on the JAX-RS endpoints in this PoC.
  - Error handling returns coarse status strings from the OUT params.

fileName: Mobile, Loyalty and the Abandoned User Service.md
content:
Mobile / Loyalty Integrations and the Abandoned User Service

=== MOBILE PUSH NOTIFICATIONS (PLANNED / STUB) ===
Direction: Outbound (BurgerQuick -> mobile devices), via a push provider TBD.
Status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. 
Detail: LOYALTY_PKG.sync_mobile_points(p_cust_id, p_device_token) is intended to push the customer's updated points balance to their phone. The code comment states: 'In the real app this would push to the mobile device via push notification.' Today it only stores the device token:
  UPDATE MOBILE_SESSIONS SET device_token = p_device_token WHERE cust_id = ... AND is_active = 1;
So a device_token is captured (the hook for FCM/APNs) but no push provider (Firebase Cloud Messaging / Apple Push) is wired. This is a future integration point.
Source: Model/database/2012_loyalty_mobile/02_loyalty_pkg.sql, 03_p_mobile_ops.sql (MOBILE_SESSIONS).

=== MOBILE SESSIONS ===
p_MobileOps records mobile logins in MOBILE_SESSIONS (session_id, cust_id, device_type, login_time, ip_address, device_token). This is the data backbone any future push or analytics integration would build on.

=== ABANDONED: USER_SERVICE MICROSERVICE (2018, DEAD) ===
Direction: was to be inbound REST (clients -> User Service).
Status: ABANDONED. Schema only; no data, no live traffic, no relationship to the real EMPLOYEES/CUSTOMERS tables.
Detail: The 2018 CTO's plan to split the monolith. A clean normalized schema (USERS with UUID PKs, bcrypt hashes, USER_ROLES junction) was created to own all user/customer/employee identity and expose it via REST. The data migration from the legacy tables (SHA-256 -> bcrypt re-hash, forced password resets) was rejected by the PM and the project died in August 2018.
MIGRATION STUB: migrate_users_to_new_schema (all TODOs, never implemented).
Source: Model/database/2018_modernization/02_abandoned_microservice.sql.
Inventory note: list as a DECOMMISSIONED / NEVER-LAUNCHED integration so it is not mistaken for a live identity provider.
